# Known answers for the `git-workflow` graders

The replies below have fixed verdicts, against which the judge of an `llm` grader is
checked before a suite's numbers are trusted. Each file is the whole reply, as the model
would send it to the prompt of the case named beside it. Each case carries one scoring
grader of its own, and the Rule column names the rule that grader measures, against the
section of the skill its rubric quotes.

| File | Case | Grader | Rule | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `records-it-with-fixup-amend.md` | `fix-that-changes-the-message` | `the-target-carries-the-fix-and-its-message` | a fix changing what its target says leaves the target carrying the change and a message true of it | PASS | the reply records the fix with `git commit --fixup=amend:a1b2c3d` and changes the message to five attempts |
| `records-it-with-plain-fixup.md` | `fix-that-changes-the-message` | `the-target-carries-the-fix-and-its-message` | a fix changing what its target says leaves the target carrying the change and a message true of it | FAIL | the reply folds a plain `git commit --fixup=a1b2c3d` with no step changing the message, which keeps it saying three attempts |
| `rewords-the-target-in-the-rebase.md` | `fix-that-changes-the-message` | `the-target-carries-the-fix-and-its-message` | a fix changing what its target says leaves the target carrying the change and a message true of it | PASS | the reply records a plain fixup and marks `a1b2c3d` `reword` in the rebase that folds it, giving the message five attempts |
| `amends-the-tip.md` | `fix-that-changes-the-message` | `the-target-carries-the-fix-and-its-message` | a fix changing what its target says leaves the target carrying the change and a message true of it | FAIL | the reply runs `git commit --amend`, which puts the change into `0718293` |
| `fetches-and-rebases-onto-origin-main.md` | `rebase-onto-a-stale-target` | `rebases-onto-the-fetched-target` | the rebase lands on the remote target's tip, fetched first | PASS | the reply fetches from `origin` and rebases onto `origin/main` |
| `rebases-onto-the-stale-main.md` | `rebase-onto-a-stale-target` | `rebases-onto-the-fetched-target` | the rebase lands on the remote target's tip, fetched first | FAIL | the reply rebases onto the local `main` with no fetch or pull before it |
| `cherry-picks-the-fetched-commit.md` | `push-after-a-fetch` | `keeps-the-fetched-commit-on-origin` | the branch sent to `origin` carries the commit a fetch brought in | PASS | the reply cherry-picks `04de0b4..e3f0903` onto the branch, then pushes under the lease |
| `pushes-with-the-lease-after-the-fetch.md` | `push-after-a-fetch` | `keeps-the-fetched-commit-on-origin` | the branch sent to `origin` carries the commit a fetch brought in | FAIL | the reply pushes under `--force-with-lease` alone, which after the fetch replaces `e3f0903` on `origin` |
| `merges-with-a-message-file.md` | `merge-message-with-no-terminal` | `names-the-merge-message` | the merge command records the merge commit with a message the reply gives, with no terminal | PASS | the reply's merge command carries `-F` naming a file holding the subject and the body |
| `merges-with-the-default-message.md` | `merge-message-with-no-terminal` | `names-the-merge-message` | the merge command records the merge commit with a message the reply gives, with no terminal | FAIL | the reply leaves the message to an editor no terminal opens, so the merge commit carries git's default message |
| `merges-then-amends-the-message.md` | `merge-message-with-no-terminal` | `names-the-merge-message` | the merge command records the merge commit with a message the reply gives, with no terminal | FAIL | the reply merges with the default message and gives its own only through `git commit --amend`, a further commit on `main` that a protection of the shared branch may refuse |
| `tags-the-merge-commit.md` | `release-tag` | `publishes-an-annotated-tag-on-the-merge-commit` | `origin` carries `main` with the merge commit and an annotated tag naming it | PASS | the reply runs `git push`, then makes an annotated tag naming the merge commit `git rev-list` finds, then runs `git push --tags` as a push of its own |
| `pushes-the-tag-by-name.md` | `release-tag` | `publishes-an-annotated-tag-on-the-merge-commit` | `origin` carries `main` with the merge commit and an annotated tag naming it | PASS | the reply pushes `main`, then makes an annotated tag naming the merge commit `git rev-list` finds, then pushes `v2.4.0` alone with `git push origin v2.4.0` |
| `tags-main-naming-no-commit.md` | `release-tag` | `publishes-an-annotated-tag-on-the-merge-commit` | `origin` carries `main` with the merge commit and an annotated tag naming it | PASS | the reply pushes `main`, then makes an annotated tag naming no commit while `HEAD` stands on the merge commit, so the tag names it, and pushes the tag |
| `tags-it-lightweight.md` | `release-tag` | `publishes-an-annotated-tag-on-the-merge-commit` | `origin` carries `main` with the merge commit and an annotated tag naming it | FAIL | the reply pushes `main`, tags the merge commit and pushes the tag alone, but `git tag v2.4.0` makes a lightweight tag |
| `tags-the-bump-commit-and-follows-tags.md` | `release-tag` | `publishes-an-annotated-tag-on-the-merge-commit` | `origin` carries `main` with the merge commit and an annotated tag naming it | FAIL | the reply tags the bump commit before the merge and publishes it under `--follow-tags`, inside the push of `main` |
| `tags-before-pushing-main.md` | `release-tag` | `publishes-an-annotated-tag-on-the-merge-commit` | `origin` carries `main` with the merge commit and an annotated tag naming it | PASS | the reply makes an annotated tag on the merge commit before `git push origin main`, then pushes the tag; `origin` ends carrying both |

| `diffs-from-the-merge-base.md` | `second-review-round` | `reads-the-round-from-the-merge-base-and-range-diff` | a round is read from the merge base of the branch and the target fetched, or pulled where the local target is named, two rounds through `range-diff` against that target | PASS | the reply reads the round with the diff naming `git merge-base origin/main <new tip>` as its left side and the new tip as its right, and compares the rounds with `git range-diff` naming both ranges |
| `diffs-two-dots-and-endpoints.md` | `second-review-round` | `reads-the-round-from-the-merge-base-and-range-diff` | a round is read from the merge base of the branch and the target fetched, or pulled where the local target is named, two rounds through `range-diff` against that target | FAIL | the reply reads the round with a two-dot diff and compares the rounds by diffing the old tip against the new one |
| `lists-and-cherry-picks-the-other-commit.md` | `push-refused-after-another-push` | `carries-the-other-commit-before-the-push` | after the lease refusal, the commit pushed from elsewhere reaches the rebased branch before a push able to overwrite it, and no commit from before the rebase comes back | PASS | the reply lists the commit the branch never held through its reflog, cherry-picks it, and pushes under `--force-with-lease` alone |
| `fetches-and-forces-with-lease.md` | `push-refused-after-another-push` | `carries-the-other-commit-before-the-push` | after the lease refusal, the commit pushed from elsewhere reaches the rebased branch before a push able to overwrite it, and no commit from before the rebase comes back | FAIL | the reply fetches and pushes under the lease, which replaces the other commit on `origin` |
| `merges-the-remote-branch.md` | `push-refused-after-another-push` | `carries-the-other-commit-before-the-push` | after the lease refusal, the commit pushed from elsewhere reaches the rebased branch before a push able to overwrite it, and no commit from before the rebase comes back | FAIL | the reply merges the remote branch in, which brings back the commits from before the rebase |
| `cherry-picks-then-repeats-the-push.md` | `push-refused-after-another-push` | `carries-the-other-commit-before-the-push` | after the lease refusal, the commit pushed from elsewhere reaches the rebased branch before a push able to overwrite it, and no commit from before the rebase comes back | FAIL | the reply cherry-picks the commit but keeps `--force-if-includes`, so the push is refused again and nothing is sent |
| `pulls-with-rebase.md` | `push-refused-after-another-push` | `carries-the-other-commit-before-the-push` | after the lease refusal, the commit pushed from elsewhere reaches the rebased branch before a push able to overwrite it, and no commit from before the rebase comes back | FAIL | the reply runs `git pull --rebase` of the branch, which copies the commits of `main` onto the old branch |
| `rewords-through-a-message-file.md` | `correction-with-no-terminal` | `rewords-the-commit-with-no-editor` | with no terminal, a message below the tip is corrected with no command waiting on an editor | PASS | the reply writes a file opening with the `amend!` line, records `--fixup=reword:` under `GIT_EDITOR='cp <file>'` and folds it with both editor variables set to `:` |
| `opens-an-interactive-rebase.md` | `correction-with-no-terminal` | `rewords-the-commit-with-no-editor` | with no terminal, a message below the tip is corrected with no command waiting on an editor | FAIL | the reply runs `git rebase -i` and edits the todo list and the message in an editor no terminal opens |
| `copies-a-file-with-no-amend-line.md` | `correction-with-no-terminal` | `rewords-the-commit-with-no-editor` | with no terminal, a message below the tip is corrected with no command waiting on an editor | FAIL | the file `cp` copies has no `amend!` line, so the rebase folds nothing and `5e1f2a0` keeps `delay` |
| `branches-from-where-the-tree-stands.md` | `commit-on-main-with-edits` | `records-the-fix-on-a-new-branch` | on a shared branch with an uncommitted change, the working branch is made from where the tree stands | PASS | the reply makes the working branch with no start point, carrying the edit, and commits there |
| `pulls-main-first.md` | `commit-on-main-with-edits` | `records-the-fix-on-a-new-branch` | on a shared branch with an uncommitted change, the working branch is made from where the tree stands | FAIL | the reply runs `git pull --ff-only` first, which git refuses with the edit in the tree, so the chain records nothing |
| `commits-on-main.md` | `commit-on-main-with-edits` | `records-the-fix-on-a-new-branch` | on a shared branch with an uncommitted change, the working branch is made from where the tree stands | FAIL | the reply commits the fix on `main` |
| `pulls-main-and-deletes-again.md` | `branch-removal-refused` | `loses-no-commit-of-the-branch` | a commit the branch alone carries is not lost to the removal | PASS | the reply fast-forwards `main` and runs `git branch -d` again, which still refuses on the unpushed docs commit, so the branch and the commit stay |
| `forces-the-deletion.md` | `branch-removal-refused` | `loses-no-commit-of-the-branch` | a commit the branch alone carries is not lost to the removal | FAIL | the reply runs `git branch -D`, which removes the unpushed docs commit with the branch |
| `checks-with-cherry-then-forces.md` | `branch-removal-refused` | `loses-no-commit-of-the-branch` | a commit the branch alone carries is not lost to the removal | FAIL | the reply chains `git branch -D` after `git cherry`, which exits 0 with the docs commit printed, so the commit is removed |
| `pushes-the-rebase-then-merges.md` | `forge-merge-of-stale-branch` | `merges-the-rebased-branch` | the merge on the forge takes the rebased commits | PASS | the reply pushes the rebased branch, then merges with `gh pr merge 18 --merge`, so GitHub merges the rebased commits |
| `merges-straight-away.md` | `forge-merge-of-stale-branch` | `merges-the-rebased-branch` | the merge on the forge takes the rebased commits | FAIL | the reply merges with no push, so GitHub merges the branch from before the rebase |
| `stops-at-the-check.md` | `forge-merge-of-stale-branch` | `merges-the-rebased-branch` | the merge on the forge takes the rebased commits | FAIL | the reply checks the branch on `origin` with no push before it, so the chain stops and the user gets no merge |

What a run without the skill is expected to do on each case, which that case's FAIL
fixture mirrors:

- `fix-that-changes-the-message`: fold a plain `--fixup` with no step changing the message, or record the fix with `--amend`, which rewrites the tip commit;
- `rebase-onto-a-stale-target`: rebase onto the local `main` without fetching;
- `push-after-a-fetch`: send the branch under the lease, which the fetch has just made match the remote;
- `merge-message-with-no-terminal`: run the merge with no message and leave it to an editor;
- `release-tag`: make a lightweight tag, or tag the bump commit before the merge;
- `second-review-round`: read the round with a two-dot diff, or compare the rounds by diffing the two tips;
- `push-refused-after-another-push`: fetch and push under the lease, merge the remote branch in, or keep `--force-if-includes` after a cherry-pick;
- `correction-with-no-terminal`: open an interactive rebase, or copy a message file with no `amend!` line;
- `commit-on-main-with-edits`: commit on `main`, or pull `main` first with the edit in the tree;
- `branch-removal-refused`: run `git branch -D` on the refusal, removing the unpushed commit;
- `forge-merge-of-stale-branch`: merge on GitHub with the rebase not pushed.

The readings no known answer checks:

- on `fix-that-changes-the-message`, an interactive rebase stopping at `a1b2c3d` to amend it, the staged change set aside first, which passes;
- on `rebase-onto-a-stale-target`, `git pull --ff-only` on `main` followed by a rebase onto `main`, and `git pull --rebase origin main` on the branch, both of which pass;
- on `push-after-a-fetch`, a reply pushing under both flags first and cherry-picking once git refuses, which passes, and one pushing under `--force`, which fails;
- on `merge-message-with-no-terminal`, a merge command carrying `-m` with the subject and a second `-m` with the body, which passes, and one carrying `--no-edit`, which fails;
- on `release-tag`, one push carrying `main` and the annotated tag together, such as `git push origin main v2.4.0`, which passes, a tag made under `-s` with a message, which passes, and `git tag -a v2.4.0 -m "Release 2.4.0" main` right after the merge with nothing merged since, `main` then standing on the merge commit, which names that commit and passes;
- on `second-review-round`, a diff from the merge base naming no tip, `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main <tip>)`, which reads the working tree and fails, and `git range-diff origin/main 4f1e2d9 <new tip>`, the command's three-argument form, which names both ranges and passes;
- on `second-review-round`, a three-dot diff or a `git range-diff` against the local `main` with no pull of `main` before it, which reads the twelve commits of other people as part of the round and fails, and the same after `git pull --ff-only` run on `main`, which passes.

A check runs the replies as cases of a throwaway plugin root, built outside this tree,
whose `prompt.md` file asks the model to output one file verbatim and whose `graders/`
directory holds a copy of every grader under test. They sit here rather than under
`evals/`, which the case walk would run as cases of the suites themselves.
